content.thinking:
I'm checking the claims against the findings: the root cause is that basket_total sets no timeout on the io-pricing call, so every account page waits out the full call, and the fallback never triggers because a slow answer doesn't raise PricingServiceFailed. That root cause rests on a reading I haven't verified yet, and the U1 reference covers the _the_basket_for calls.

I'm checking whether the io-pricing slowdown explains the account page load times, and whether the alert fired late. The pricing service's slow answers look like the likely cause, which the findings support but haven't fully confirmed. I'm also tracing the latency rise and the onset window of the slow calls.

I'm checking that the io-pricing calls at about 1500ms each are the owner's service and that the restart confirmed the source, and that the account pages were waiting on that same call. Code-Fix's reading also says two existing tests expected a slow answer to come back as a price, and I'm noting no review or test check that would have caught it.

I'm going through the remaining claims against the record: the went-wrong note about nobody being paged, and whether the root cause's specific 1500ms figure from the io-pricing calls starting at 23:12 holds up. Both check out against the cited sources, so I'm not flagging anything in this stretch.

supported.quote: basket_total, which _the_basket_for calls to fetch the account page's optional basket total, sets no limit on how long it waits for io-pricing, so when io-pricing's basket-total calls began taking {G9feb.1}, every account page waited out the whole call.

The page's existing fallback, which renders it without the total, only runs on PricingServiceFailed, and a slow answer never raises that. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.

A pricing service the shop asks for each shopper's basket total began answering slowly, and the shop's account pages likely waited for it with no time limit, even though they can be shown without that total.
If io-pricing slows down again, every account page could again slow down by the same amount.
rows: AI-2 (prevent, open): Review and merge the proposed fix

supported.quote: The latency of io-shop's slowest requests rose past the alert's line and stayed there until the alert fired.
rows: The alert came 6 minutes 5 seconds after its series passed its line

supported.quote: From the onset, io-shop's calls to io-pricing for each shopper's basket total took {G9feb.1} each, logged as slow upstream calls over {G9feb.5}.
The slowness came from io-pricing, the internal service owned by checkout-platform.

Each account page waited for that call to finish. _the_basket_for calls basket_total on the page's path, and basket_total sets no limit on how long it waits, so a slow answer was waited out in full instead of failing over to the page's existing fallback without the total.
No review or test check was seen that requires calls from io-shop to its dependencies to have a time limit.
Code-Fix's reading says io-shop's existing tests expected a slow pricing answer to come back as a price.

io-pricing's slowdown was found only by io-shop's latency alert. No alert on io-pricing's own latency was seen, and nothing was seen alerting on the slow-upstream-call warnings io-shop logged from the onset.
Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to the alert.
rows: Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.
